note: Frozen eval subset: never feeds the fine-tune query distribution.

queries.query: Bruno's distinction between two sorts of frenzy: a blind bestial madness, and a divinely inspired rapture that lifts a person above ordinary humanity
queries.note: The two kinds of enthusiasts opening the Third Dialogue; 'stupidity and irrational impetuosity', 'divine abstraction', 'black bile' paraphrased away; 'Bruno' kept as the author any reader knows.

queries.query: the heroic lover's soul torn by simultaneous opposites, frozen expectation and blazing longing at once, silent yet filling the air with cries
queries.note: The standard-bearer sonnet and its gloss in the Second Dialogue; 'my hopes are ice and my desires glowing', 'tremble, sparkle, freeze, and burn' paraphrased into different words.

queries.query: the paradox of the chase after divine truth in which the pursuer is captured and turned into the very quarry he was hunting
queries.note: The hunter-becomes-the-hunted passage (the Actaeon theme) in Part 2; 'the thief becomes the thing stolen', 'fugitive and wild body', 'mouth of his own intelligence' paraphrased away.

queries.query: the tale of nine young men struck sightless by love, each giving a different cause for his blindness, who wander for years before reaching the nymphs of a British island
queries.note: The nine blind men of the Fourth and Fifth Dialogues of Part 2; 'ploughed the seas', 'temperate sky of the British Isles', 'lovely graceful nymph' paraphrased; the nine blind men kept as the episode any reader of the work knows.

queries.query: is ecstatic love or divine madness a genuine path to knowledge of God
queries.note: The whole book answers this, but so do Sufi, bhakti, and Platonic traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: how can love of visible beauty become a ladder toward the divine
queries.note: Material beauty as a glittering ray of spiritual form; the eros-ascent is answered across many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
